##### Summary
Fixes #7804 

We verified a necessity to bring an integer value that will be used to define the stream version, considering all changes that will come with labels and other subjects, this PR brings this variable to the handshake.
##### Component Name
stream
##### Additional Information
To test this PR it was used:

- This current PR
- A PR with the previous version of the stream protocol
- Netdata 1.14 to be sure that we had the first version(The `Hit me baby` version).

#### Running agent with latest version and having slave connect:

- With old netdata
   - we get the old protocol negotiation **Hit me baby, push them over...**
- With current version
   - we get the host labels protocol negotiation **Hit me baby, push them over and bring the host labels...**

issue_context.title: Change the streaming protocol to allow forward-compatability.
issue_context.body:
##### Description
During the testing of the PR for issue #7488 we discovered that the new division of `system_info` into `HOST_` and `CONTAINER_` labels is incompatible with the design of the streaming protocol. The handshake for a stream connection names the structure fields as parameters in the initial request.

To change this we need to introduce a new version of the streaming protocol that transfers the two sets of labels. Unfortunately we have discovered that the changes in issue #7549 that were meant to allow forward-compatibility in the streaming protocol are not forward-compatible with further changes.

The basic problem is that the protocol message must be one of two exact strings to avoid the connection being aborted and there is no way to put a version number in the strings.

To move forward we need to redesign the streaming protocol handshake so that it is forward-compatible (and also backwards compatible with the recent changes).

#### Summary

Originally the startup message "Hit me baby, one more time..." from master to slave was used as a protocol discriminator. After #7549 it is acting as a version discriminator and hosts will disconnect when they do not recognize the message.

The protocol will be updated to perform agreement of highest compatible version during handshake. For simplicity we will switch to integer protocol versions, using the following scheme:

```
0 - original
1 - host labels
2 - host labels + docker labels
3 - host labels + docker labels + chart labels
```

The advantage of integer numbering over a bitmask scheme is that we can depend on grouping of features after negotiation, which leads to simpler code. We need to handle the three schemes in a backwards compatible way:

```
1. old slave                      -> no "NETDATA_PROTOCOL_VERSION"
2. slave with the patch #7549     -> NETDATA_PROTOCOL_VERSION=1.1
3. new slave                      -> ver=2&...
```

```
A. old master                -> "Hit me baby, one more time..."
B. master with the patch     -> "... with host labels"
C. new master               -> negotiate according to psuedo-code

master_version = 2;
if ('ver=n' was in the url  ) {
  "Hit me with your rhythm stick: %d" % min(n,master_version)
  use_version = n;
} else {
  "Hit me baby, one more time..."
   version = 0;
}
```

Falling back to the lowest version fixes a current incompatibility with systems from before patch #7549. On the client side we can map the response string back to the negotiated version.
comments: I've put some temporary code in rrdpush so that we can get issue #7488 finished and unblock other tasks. A better approach (which should be implemented in this task) is to check the `NETDATA_SYSTEM_CONTAINER_DETECTION` value on a stream from an old version, if it is set to "none" or "unknown" then rename the six `NETDATA_SYSTEM_*` variables as `NETDATA_HOST_*` - *otherwise' rename them as `NETDATA_CONTAINER_*`. This will produce the most accurate metadata data when old versions stream to a newer host.

I think this is the "in between" protocol version that simply sets the NETDATA_PROTOCOL_VERSION and its out there now -- it is ignored if a `ver` is present during the stream establishment
The original idea was to have conditions to use versions like the kernel version, but after a talk with Andrew we moved it to an integer version, so as @stelfrag said this is between stream versions.
There are identical messages that the slave uses an old Netdata but the check has been changed to START_STREAMING_V2

The beginning is 100% equal, and this was done to create "message compatibility" (It is between quotes, because I think I generalized the concept ).
The system won't fail when do these kind of tests, because we are using `memcmp` with the length we want to compare.
Finally, we have this order, because I hope, that in a short period of time, nobody will use the oldest Netdata stream protocol.
But we are trying to negotiate the highest version that both ends understand?
For while yes, but when we begin to move from protocol version 2 in front, we will use the algorithm specified in the issue 7804.
